angle: Behavioural design for a daily habit: the unit of reading, the trigger, the reward, the grace, the identity language, the return visit — applied to a man whose job is the Bible and whose personal reading is the first thing his job eats.
thesis: A pastor already knows how to study; what he loses is his own morning. So the pastor path must do exactly two things well: open on a reading that is his, not his congregation's, and make his study work accrue instead of evaporate. Today the app does the opposite at both ends — the first card on his Home is a door OUT of the app to sermon prep (it sits above the reading), and the one-tap "To sermon" capture files into a bag with no visible inbox anywhere in the live app (SermonWorkspace and PreachScreen are built, tested and deliberately unmounted). Fixing those two, plus framing the AI as the research assistant it actually is and putting the source-and-licence line where he can see it before he quotes it from a pulpit, is the whole design. Everything else on this path already works and stays.
principles: His time first, his job second. The top of Home is reading + one prompt; every piece of sermon work sits below it. The live greeting already promises this — 'This is your time — not ministry, just you and God' — and the layout currently contradicts it (Preach card renders at HomeScreen.tsx:2106, above the hero plate at ~2263).

Never an empty hero. The PASTOR_CHAPTERS day-one floor is the zero-decision first move; 'don't know where to start' is universal, and three-fifths of the people who say it have followed Christ 20+ years (research, cross-cutting #2).

The unit is one chapter and one question. Busyness is the #1 reason reading declines (40-58%); ~70% of pastors already spend 8+ hours a week on prep. His devotional unit must be smaller than his study, and visibly separate from it.
Work accrues. Every capture, every focus line, every outline is visible, countable and reusable next week. A bag he cannot see is not a habit loop.

The AI finds; he writes. 79% of pastors worry AI could replace God's role, 63% that it could replace pastoral leadership, and 71% are cautious. The framing sentence is the highest-leverage copy change in this path.
Only real numbers. Campus Overview already refuses to fabricate; the same rule governs the weekly line and any time-saved claim.
Grace is named, not just applied. The streak freeze already bridges one missed day silently — say it once, plainly, because guilt-framed streaks drive opt-out and uninstall.
Nothing new gets its own full-screen surface. The Preach hand-off off-app is his 9 Sep ruling and is pinned by tests; the fix is a strip on Home, not a revived workspace.

journey.day0: Cold device auto-defaults to new_to_faith and shows Day1Landing. He taps the quiet 'Not new to faith? Choose your path' line, gets the one sheet, taps 'I'm a pastor and I teach and preach' — one tap saves (source 'onboarding') and opens Home (ChoosePathSheet.tsx:161-175). Home opens on a reading with no plan set up: PASTOR_CHAPTERS[localDayIndex()] — persona-gated and credit-free, bypassing handleRead so nothing is credited to a plan day. PathArrivalStrip names where he is and offers 'Sign in for campus tools'. The set-up wizard offers 'Help me pick' (3 questions) or 'I know what I want' (straight to Plans, wizard permanently done). Nothing asks him to do sermon work.
journey.first_session: One chapter, already open. He reads, and directly under it Between You & God asks one leadership question from the 15-prompt set. That is the whole session — five minutes. If he highlights something, the toolbar offers 'To sermon' and the capture appears immediately in This week's prep below the prompt, with a count. First session success = he read something for himself, not that he prepped.
journey.return_visit: Days 2-5: same shape, new chapter from the rotation or his chosen plan. The prep strip now shows 2-4 filed verses and his preaching focus line. The Preach card sits below all of it, unchanged in copy and destination. He sets his reminder hour once, or the app infers it from when he actually opens after 5-7 sessions.
journey.week2: The strip has enough in it to be worth acting on: 'Build an outline from these' sends his own captures to Bible AI in the pinned outline shape (big idea, three points, one weekly action) — and the button says 'Built from your 8 filed verses' so the source is never in doubt. This is also the week he first taps 'Where this comes from' under a commentary, before quoting it on Sunday. Monday morning of week 2, Your Week shows counted facts from the 60-day behaviour log: mornings in the Word, verses filed, outlines started, and one question that joins the reading to the preaching.
journey.missed_day: The existing freeze bridges a single missed day and the count keeps going. The only change: when a freeze was actually spent today, one plain line under the greeting says so — 'You missed yesterday. Your streak's still here.' On a real reset, 'New start today. Your best run was 34 days.' (bestCount already survives a reset, streak.ts:30/80.) No red, no fire, no exclamation, no push that mentions a streak at all.
journey.seasonal: His preaching focus IS the season for this persona — one editable line that flows into every pastor AI prompt (buildPastorPrompt ctx.focus). Church-wide moments (New Year, Lent, a Futures series) reach him as a real campus number in Campus Overview, never a seeded one. Turning his own series into a campus-wide plan is the seasonal build the research points at (calendar moments drive every spike) and is an owner decision, not part of this design.

comfort_access: One quiet line directly under Between You & God: "Hard week? Read the comfort verses." It opens the day's comfort chapter (COMFORT_CHAPTERS rotation) in the reading surface with the comfort toolbar — Note and Close only — and a foot line that says "Your path hasn't changed." It must never write dw_setup, never call saveSetup, never stamp a source, never credit a plan day, and never show a graduation prompt. It is also repeated once in More. This persona is where the cross-path comfort tap matters most: 65% of pastors report loneliness (up from 42% in 2015) and 38% considered quitting in the past year, and crisis is not a persona anyone chooses on a good day. The global persistent tap across all five paths is the research's own build #2 and belongs to that build; this design only guarantees the line exists on his screen.
reminders: One a day, at the hour he actually opens, in neutral scripture language, never mentioning a streak. Default stays 7am until the behaviour log has 5-7 sessions, then offer the inferred hour once: "You usually open around 6am. Want the reminder then?" — asked once, never repeated if declined. No reminder on Sunday for pastor_leader (his working day; inference, not sourced — flagged as an owner decision). Opt-out is one tap in More and is remembered. The freeze already covers a single missed day; the app says so once in plain words instead of sending a rescue push. Push copy stays in the existing EN/ID templates; ES/PT have no push templates at all today, which is a gap for Futuros pastors.
instrumentation: pastor_capture (detail: persona|ref) — a 'To sermon' tap. Proves the capture loop is real, and is the leading indicator for week-2 return.
pastor_prep_open (detail: persona|item_count) — the prep strip expanded or an item opened. Answers whether the inbox was the missing half of the loop.
pastor_outline (detail: persona|item_count) — the outline prompt sent. The conversion metric for capture → use.
preach_handoff (detail: persona|has_focus|item_count) — the Preach card tap. Read against pastor_outline it settles the open question of whether prep should ever come back in-app.
pastor_focus_set (detail: persona) — the preaching focus edited outside the wizard. Proves the self-serve lever is used, not just shipped.
trust_panel_open (detail: persona|source) — 'Where this comes from'. The research's own test: trust-panel visibility against session length.
comfort_tap (detail: persona) — the 'Hard week?' line, cut by originating persona. A duty-of-care metric, not a growth metric; watch it, never optimise it upward.
reminder_opt_out (detail: persona|days_active) — the shame check. If it rises after any streak or reminder copy change, revert that change.
streak_repair_shown (detail: persona) — the grace line rendered. Pair with next-day return to test whether naming grace beats leaving it silent.

Persona on every existing event. daily_reading, app_open, chat_message, plan_start and push_subscribe must all carry persona in detail, or D1/D7/D30 cannot be cut by path — and no public source will ever supply those numbers (research build #1).

One nightly rollup: reads per path per day, D1/D7/D30 by path, median session length, completion rate, reminder opt-out rate. Descriptive only; nothing on screen is driven by it without a further decision.
self_serve_levers: Preaching focus — one editable field on the prep strip (dw_sermon_prep_focus). Changes what every pastor AI prompt is anchored to. Today it is asked once in wizard step 13 and then unreachable, because the only editor is the unmounted SermonWorkspace.
The prep bag itself — file with 'To sermon' while reading, remove per item, copy all out. No developer, no admin.
Reading plan — the full catalogue on the Plans tab, any plan, any time; the wizard's 'I know what I want' goes straight there.
Campus code — typed by hand or provisioned at staff sign-in; decides whose real numbers Campus Overview shows. Nothing is fabricated when it is absent.
Campus chip (HomeContextChips) — his campus, applied on tap, no Settings trip.
Congregation chooser — which church's sermon notes the notes surfaces use.
Reminder hour and push on/off — More → Notifications.
Path — PathSwatch in the Home header, any time, no lock for a signed-in pastor.
Study sources — the trust sheet is entirely data-driven from the study_* tables via study.js?sources=1, so adding or removing a source updates what he sees with no code change and no deploy.

NOT self-serve today, and worth saying so plainly: the 30-chapter pastor rotation, the 15 reflection prompts, the wizard's recommended plans, push copy, and the two milestone lists are all hardcoded. The one worth moving is the rotation plus the prompts, to /books/pastor-rotation.json — network-first already, so an edit reaches returning users, provided CACHE_NAME/STATIC_CACHE and SW_VERSION are bumped together. The rest should stay in code.

Sync: dw_sermon_prep and dw_sermon_prep_focus ride the misc bag. Every write must merge from what is currently in localStorage and never rebuild from React state, and must call pushNow via syncMisc — otherwise a second device's captures get overwritten by stale mount-time state.

Date axis: counting days from behavior.ts requires moving it off UTC toISOString to toLocaleDateString('en-CA') first. Existing records stay comparable (both YYYY-MM-DD) but events near midnight shift by a day once.

Adding persona to push_subscriptions is a schema change — migration in the repo, and push cannot be verified on a deploy preview at all (pushSupported only allowlists futuresdailyword.com, www and localhost). Verify on localhost or prod.
If the pastor rotation or prompts move to /books/*.json, bump CACHE_NAME/STATIC_CACHE and SW_VERSION together, or returning users keep the old bytes.
Do not let 'give the bag an inbox' turn into reviving PreachScreen/SermonWorkspace. That reverses your 9 Sep decision and two tests will say so.

The prep strip adds a card to a screen you have already called 'completely stripped' once when it lost richness. This adds material below the reading and removes nothing above it — but check it at 390px in both themes before it merges.
